nodes.name: Every matrix is a sum of a normal and a nilpotent matrix
nodes.statement: Alternatively, there exists a basis in $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that the matrix of the operator $T$ with respect to this basis is upper-triangular. Taking the diagonal part $N$ of the operator $T$ in this basis, we obtain a normal operator. The difference $T-N$ is, obviously, a strictly upper-triangular matrix. Every strictly upper-triangular matrix is, clearly, nilpotent. Thus, an arbitrary matrix is a sum of a normal matrix and nilpotent matrix.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonal part of a Schur triangularization is normal and the remainder is nilpotent, so every matrix is normal plus nilpotent.
assumptions: Alternatively, there exists a basis in $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that the matrix of the operator $T$ with respect to this basis is upper-triangular.
conclusions: Thus, an arbitrary matrix is a sum of a normal matrix and nilpotent matrix.

nodes.name: Ringrose's theorem
nodes.statement: For every compact operator $T\in B(H),$ there exists an increasing net of projections $p_{\lambda}$, $\lambda\in[0,1]$, with $p_0=0$ and $p_1=1$, such that, letting $p_{\lambda-0}=\vee_{\mu<\lambda}\,p_\mu,$ \begin{enumerate}[{\rm (a)}] \item $Tp_{\lambda}=p_{\lambda}Tp_{\lambda}$ for all $\lambda\in[0,1].$ \item for every $\lambda\in(0,1]$ either $p_{\lambda}=p_{\lambda-0}$ or $p_{\lambda}-p_{\lambda-0}$ is a one-dimensional projection. \end{enumerate} Furthermore, if for such a family we have $Tp_{\lambda}=p_{\lambda-0}Tp_{\lambda}$ for all $\lambda\in(0,1],$ then $T$ is quasinilpotent.
nodes.statement_short: Every compact operator admits an increasing nest of projections with at most one-dimensional jumps that triangularizes it; strict triangularity forces quasinilpotency.

nodes.statement: For every compact operator $T\in B(H),$ there exist a normal operator $N$ and a quasinilpotent operator $Q$ such that $T=N+Q.$
assumptions: For every compact operator $T\in B(H),$

nodes.name: Proof of the Ringrose decomposition corollary
nodes.statement: Indeed, set $$N=\sum_{p_{\lambda}\neq p_{\lambda-0}}(p_{\lambda}-p_{\lambda-0})T(p_{\lambda}-p_{\lambda-0}),\quad Q=T-N,$$ where the sum (of pairwise orthogonal $1-$dimensional operators) converges in strong operator topology. It is clear that $N$ is normal and that $Qp_{\lambda}=p_{\lambda-0}Qp_{\lambda}.$ In particular, it follows from Theorem \ref{ringrose} that $Q$ is quasinilpotent.

nodes.name: Loosening the II$_1$--factor hypothesis to diffuse finite algebras
nodes.statement: In the above theorem, the hypothesis that $\mathcal{M}$ be a II$_1$--factor and $\tau$ its tracial state can clearly be loosened to require only that $\mathcal{M}$ be a diffuse, finite von Neumann algebra and $\tau$ be any normal, faithful, tracial state on it. This is because (a) any such $\mathcal{M}$ can be embedded, via a normal, trace-preserving $*$-homomorphism, into a II$_1$--factor (to see this, use for example Lemma~2.3 and Theorem~2.5 from~\cite{D94} to see that the free product with respect to traces of $\mathcal{M}$ with $L^\infty[0,1]$ is a II$_1$-factor) and (b) the projection onto a hyperinvariant subspace of any operator belongs to the von Neumann algebra generated by the operator (this is easy to show, but for a proof see, for example, Proposition~ 2.1 of~\cite{D05}).
nodes.statement_short: The Haagerup--Schultz theorem extends verbatim to any diffuse finite von Neumann algebra, by embedding into a II$_1$--factor and noting hyperinvariant projections lie in the generated algebra.

nodes.name: s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operator
nodes.statement: We note that the quasinilpotent operator in Ringrose's theorem is here replaced by an s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operator, which is an operator $Q$ such that $((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}$ converges in strong operator topology to $0$; in this notation (which was introduced in~\cite{DFS}) s.o.t.\ is an abbreviation for ``strong operator topology;'' that quasinilpotent operators must be s.o.t.--quasinilpotent follows from the characterization~\eqref{eq:Q*nQn} of quasinilpotency. By Theorem~8.1 of~\cite{HS2}, in a finite von Neumann algebra the s.o.t.-quasinilpotent operators are precisely those whose Brown measures are concentrated at $\{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: An operator $Q$ is s.o.t.-quasinilpotent when $((Q^*)^nQ^n)^{1/2n}\to0$ strongly, equivalently when its Brown measure sits at $0$.

nodes.name: Diagonal/upper-triangular reading of $N$ and $Q$
nodes.statement: As in Ringrose's theorem, a family $(q_t)_{0\le t\le 1}$ of $T$--invariant (in fact, $T$--hyper\-in\-vari\-ant) projections is involved in Theorem~\ref{decomposition}, and $N$ and $Q$ can be regarded as diagonal and upper triangular, respectively, with respect to this family of projections. Indeed, $N$ is obtained as the conditional expectation of $T$ onto the von Neumann algebra generated by $\{q_t\mid 0\le t\le 1\}$. However, unlike in Ringrose's theorem, the dimensions (i.e., in our finite von Neumann algebra setting, the traces) of the projections $q_t$ can take large jumps as $t$ varies. Indeed, if $T$ itself is s.o.t.-quasinilpotent, then our construction yields $N=0$ and $\{q_t\mid 0\le t\le 1\}\subseteq\{0,1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: $N$ is the conditional expectation of $T$ onto the algebra generated by the hyperinvariant nest, but unlike Ringrose's nest the traces may jump.

nodes.statement_short: The classical statement that $N$ and $T$ share eigenvalues is the compact-operator shadow of Theorem 5(b).

nodes.name: generalised singular value function
nodes.statement: For every $T\in\mathcal{M},$ the generalised singular value function $\mu(T)$, denoted $t\to\mu(t,T)$ for $t\in(0,1)$, is defined by the formula (see, e.g., \cite{FackKosaki}) $$\mu(t,T)=\inf\{\|Tp\|_{\infty}:\ p\in\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{M}),\;\tau(1-p)\leq t\}.$$ It is continuous from the right in $t.$

nodes.name: Haagerup--Schultz projections as spectral projections of the s.o.t. limit
nodes.statement: It is proved in \cite{HS2} that, for every $T\in\mathcal{M},$ $((T^*)^nT^n)^{1/2n}$ converges as $n\to\infty$ in strong operator topology. The spectral projection of the limiting operator on the interval $[0,r]$ is exactly the Haagerup--Schultz projection $p_{\mathcal{B}_r}$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:HS} corresponding to the ball $\mathcal{B}_r=\{|z|\leq r\}.$ Thus, an operator $T$ has Brown measure supported on $\{0\}$ if and only if $((T^*)^nT^n)^{1/2n}$ converges in strong operator topology to $0.$

nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{D}$ is a von Neumann subalgebra of the finite von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ with normal, faithful, tracial state $\tau$, then there exists a unique linear operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}:\mathcal{M}\to\mathcal{D}$ such that, for all $A\in\mathcal{M}$ and $B\in\mathcal{D}$, \begin{enumerate}[{\rm (a)}] \item ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(AB)={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(A)B$ \item ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(BA)=B{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(A)$ \item $\tau({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(A))=\tau(A)$. \end{enumerate} Furthermore, ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}$ is positive (in fact, completely positive), of norm $1$ and can be realised as the orthogonal projection from $\mathcal{L}_2(\mathcal{M})$ onto $\mathcal{L}_2(\mathcal{D})$ restricted to $\mathcal{M}$.

Then $${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{A}}(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{A}_n}(T),\quad(T\in\mathcal{M}),$$ where the limit is taken in the strong operator topology.
nodes.statement_short: Conditional expectations onto an increasing or decreasing sequence of subalgebras converge strongly to the expectation onto the limit algebra.

nodes.name: Construction of the nest $q_t$ and the algebra $\mathcal{D}$ from a Peano curve
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $\rho:[0,1]\to\{|z|\leq \|T\|_{\infty}\}$ be a Peano curve.\footnote{A continuous surjective mapping $[0,1]\to[0,1]^2$ was first constructed by Peano \cite{Peano}. See, for example, \cite{Man} for details. We may take the ball rather than the square since they are homeomorphic.} \begin{enumerate}[(a)] \item Set $q_t$ to be the Haagerup--Schultz projection for $T$ associated to the Borel set $\rho([0,t]).$ Then $q_t$ is increasing in $t$. Since $\tau(q_t)=\nu_T(\rho([0,t])$, we have $q_t=\wedge_{t'>t}q_{t'}$; i.e., $q_t$ is strong-operator-topology continuous from the right in $t$. \item Set $\mathcal{D}$ to be the von Neumann algebra generated by $\{q_t\mid t\in[0,1]\}.$ \item For every $n\geq0,$ set $\mathcal{D}_n$ to be the algebra generated by $q_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n.$ \end{enumerate} For technical convenience, we will assume that the Brown measure of $T$ has no atom at $\rho(0)$ (i.e. $\nu_T(\rho(0))=0$). This ensures $q_0=0$ and it can always be arranged by modification of $\rho,$ if necessary.
nodes.statement_short: Sweep a Peano curve over the spectrum-carrying disc and take the Haagerup--Schultz projections of its initial arcs as an increasing nest generating a commutative algebra $\mathcal{D}$ with dyadic subalgebras $\mathcal{D}_n$.

nodes.name: Identify the norm limit

nodes.statement_short: The strong limit is ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, so the uniform Cauchy sequence converges to it; let $m\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Why the case $\lambda=0$ does not suffice
nodes.statement: Note that one could not first prove Lemma \ref{det convergence} in the case $\lambda=0$ and then infer its assertion in full generality by applying this result to the operator $T-\lambda.$ The reason is that algebra $\mathcal{D}$ for the operator $T$ differs from that fo r the operator $T-\lambda.$
nodes.statement_short: A reduction to $\lambda=0$ fails because $\mathcal{D}$ depends on the operator, and differs for $T$ and $T-\lambda$.

nodes.name: Why the theorem does not follow directly from the proposition
nodes.statement: It is tempting to try to infer Theorem \ref{decomposition} from Proposition \ref{br equ} by applying its assertion to the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T).$ This is impossible because the algebra $\mathcal{D}$ for the operator $T$ differs from that for the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T).$

nodes.name: Relation to the Weyl lemma on logarithmic submajorization
nodes.statement: The following submajorization result is related to the Weyl lemma stating that $\lambda(T)\prec\prec_{\log}\mu(T)$ for every compact operator $T\in B(H)$ (see, e.g., Theorem II.3.1 of \cite{GK1}).

nodes.name: Logarithmic submajorization of the block-diagonal part
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$ Then $$Tp+(1-p)T\prec\prec_{\log}T.$$
nodes.statement_short: Deleting the off-diagonal corner of a triangular operator logarithmically submajorizes it.

S=\left(\begin{matrix}A&0\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),$$ with $A=Tp$ and $C=(1-p)T.$ By Lemma~\ref{boolean lemma}, there exist increasing nets $p_s\le p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(p),$ and $q_s\le 1-p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(1-p),$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s$, $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$|C|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(C))}\mu(s,C)dq_s,\quad |A^*|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(A))}\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ Choosing appropriate spectral projections of $A$ and $C$, we see that for every $t>0,$ there exist $t_1,t_2>0$ such that $t_1+t_2=t$ and such that \begin{equation} \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^{t_1}\log(\mu(s,A))ds+\int_0^{t_2}\log(\mu(s,C))ds. \end{equation} Set $$A_0=\int_0^{t_1}\mu(s,A)dp_s,\quad C_0=\int_0^{t_2}\mu(s,C)dq_s$$ and $$T_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix},\quad S_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&0\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Note that $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds.$$ We now claim that $\mu(T_0)\leq\mu(T).$ Indeed, $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix} A^*A&A^*B\\ B^*A&B^*B+C^*C \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*=\begin{pmatrix} AA^*+BB^*&BC_0\\ C_0B&C_0^2 \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*.$$ Therefore, $$\mu(T)=\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix})\geq \mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})\geq\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})=\mu(T_0).$$ Let now $r=p_{\tau({\rm supp}(C_0))}+q_{\tau({\rm supp}(A_0))}.$ Using~\eqref{det}, we get $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds=\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0))$$ and, since $\mu(rT_0r)\le\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$, we get $$\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r))\stackrel{\eqref{det}}{=}\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,rT_0r))ds\leq \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$ It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that $\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0)=\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r)$ and, therefore, $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds\leq\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$
nodes.statement_short: Cut $A$ and $C$ down to spectral pieces realizing the log-integral, compare singular values of the truncated triangular operators, and identify determinants via the block formula.

nodes.name: Block-matrix setup
nodes.statement: Let $S=Tp+(1-p)T.$ Writing elements of $\mathcal{M}$ as matrices with respect to projections $p$ and $(1-p),$ we have $$T=\left(\begin{matrix}A&B\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),\qquad S=\left(\begin{matrix}A&0\\0&C\end{matrix}\right),$$ with $A=Tp$ and $C=(1-p)T.$
nodes.statement_short: Write $T$ and $S$ as $2\times2$ block matrices with respect to $p$ and $1-p$.

nodes.name: Spectral nests for $A$ and $C$
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{boolean lemma}, there exist increasing nets $p_s\le p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(p),$ and $q_s\le 1-p,$ $0\leq s\leq\tau(1-p),$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s$, $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$|C|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(C))}\mu(s,C)dq_s,\quad |A^*|=\int_0^{\tau({\rm supp}(A))}\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$
nodes.statement_short: Get trace-parametrized nests resolving $|C|$ and $|A^*|$.

nodes.name: Split the log-integral
nodes.statement: Choosing appropriate spectral projections of $A$ and $C$, we see that for every $t>0,$ there exist $t_1,t_2>0$ such that $t_1+t_2=t$ and such that \begin{equation} \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^{t_1}\log(\mu(s,A))ds+\int_0^{t_2}\log(\mu(s,C))ds. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Pick $t_1+t_2=t$ splitting $\int_0^t\log\mu(s,S)$ across $A$ and $C$.

nodes.name: Define the truncations $T_0$ and $S_0$
nodes.statement: Set $$A_0=\int_0^{t_1}\mu(s,A)dp_s,\quad C_0=\int_0^{t_2}\mu(s,C)dq_s$$ and $$T_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix},\quad S_0=\begin{pmatrix} A_0&0\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}.$$ Note that $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds.$$
nodes.statement_short: Truncate to $A_0,C_0$ and form the triangular $T_0$ and diagonal $S_0$ with the same log-integral.

nodes.name: Singular value comparison
nodes.statement: We now claim that $\mu(T_0)\leq\mu(T).$ Indeed, $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix} A^*A&A^*B\\ B^*A&B^*B+C^*C \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*=\begin{pmatrix} AA^*+BB^*&BC_0\\ C_0B&C_0^2 \end{pmatrix}\geq\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix}^*.$$ Therefore, $$\mu(T)=\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C \end{pmatrix})\geq \mu(\begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})\geq\mu(\begin{pmatrix} A_0&B\\ 0&C_0 \end{pmatrix})=\mu(T_0).$$
nodes.statement_short: Two positivity estimates on the block products give $\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$.

nodes.name: Pass to determinants on the corner
nodes.statement: Let now $r=p_{\tau({\rm supp}(C_0))}+q_{\tau({\rm supp}(A_0))}.$ Using~\eqref{det}, we get $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds=\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S_0))ds=\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0))$$ and, since $\mu(rT_0r)\le\mu(T_0)\le\mu(T)$, we get $$\log(\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r))\stackrel{\eqref{det}}{=}\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,rT_0r))ds\leq \int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$
nodes.statement_short: Express the log-integral as $\log\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0)$ and bound $\log\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r)$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that $\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(S_0)=\Delta_{r\mathcal{M}r}(rT_0r)$ and, therefore, $$\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,S))ds\leq\int_0^t\log(\mu(s,T))ds.$$
nodes.statement_short: The triangular determinant formula equates the two determinants, giving the submajorization.

nodes.name: Determinant inequality for the diagonal part
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$ Then $$\Delta(1+\big|Tp+(1-p)T)\big|^2)\le\Delta(1+|T|^2).$$
assumptions: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $p\in\mathcal{M}$ be a projection such that $Tp=pTp.$

nodes.name: Proof of the determinant inequality
nodes.statement: Set $y=\mu(Tp+(1-p)T)$ and $x=\mu(T).$ We may without loss of generality assume $y$ is not identically $0.$ By Lemma \ref{lem:anytrace}, we have $y\prec\prec_{\log}x.$ Set $\alpha$ to be the infimum of the set $y^{-1}(\{0\}).$ Then we must have $\inf x^{-1}(\{0\})\ge\alpha.$ Let $\varepsilon_n=\min\{y(\alpha-\frac1n),x(\alpha-\frac1n)\}$ for all integers $n$ so large that $\frac1n<\alpha.$ Then the functions $$y_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}y)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},\quad x_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}x)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},$$ when nonzero, take only values $\ge0.$ Clearly, $y_n\prec\prec x_n.$ Since the function $\Phi_n:z\to\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2e^{2z})$ is convex on $[0,\infty),$ it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \begin{multline*} \int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^1\Phi_n(y_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)\\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\Phi_n(x_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)=\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*} Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain \begin{multline*} \int_0^1\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+y^2(s))ds \\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+x^2(s))ds\leq\int_0^1\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*} Now \eqref{det} finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Convert logarithmic submajorization into ordinary submajorization of truncated logarithms and apply the Hardy--Littlewood--Polya inequality with $\Phi_n(z)=\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2e^{2z})$.

nodes.name: Set up the singular value functions
nodes.statement: Set $y=\mu(Tp+(1-p)T)$ and $x=\mu(T).$ We may without loss of generality assume $y$ is not identically $0.$
nodes.statement_short: Name $y,x$ and discard the trivial case $y\equiv0$.

nodes.name: Truncation parameters
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:anytrace}, we have $y\prec\prec_{\log}x.$ Set $\alpha$ to be the infimum of the set $y^{-1}(\{0\}).$ Then we must have $\inf x^{-1}(\{0\})\ge\alpha.$ Let $\varepsilon_n=\min\{y(\alpha-\frac1n),x(\alpha-\frac1n)\}$ for all integers $n$ so large that $\frac1n<\alpha.$
nodes.statement_short: Use the previous lemma and introduce the supports' cut-off $\alpha$ and the scalars $\varepsilon_n$.

nodes.name: Nonnegative truncated logarithms
nodes.statement: Then the functions $$y_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}y)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},\quad x_n=\log(\varepsilon_n^{-1}x)\chi_{(0,\alpha-1/n)},$$ when nonzero, take only values $\ge0.$ Clearly, $y_n\prec\prec x_n.$
nodes.statement_short: The functions $y_n,x_n$ are nonnegative and satisfy $y_n\prec\prec x_n$.

nodes.name: Apply the Hardy--Littlewood--Polya inequality
nodes.statement: Since the function $\Phi_n:z\to\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2e^{2z})$ is convex on $[0,\infty),$ it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \begin{multline*} \int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^1\Phi_n(y_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)\\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\Phi_n(x_n(s))ds-(1-\alpha+\frac1n)\log(1+\varepsilon_n^2)=\int_0^{\alpha-1/n}\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\Phi_n$ transfers the submajorization to the log-integrals.

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain \begin{multline*} \int_0^1\log(1+y^2(s))ds=\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+y^2(s))ds \\ \leq\int_0^{\alpha}\log(1+x^2(s))ds\leq\int_0^1\log(1+x^2(s))ds. \end{multline*} Now \eqref{det} finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Let $n\to\infty$ and rewrite via the determinant formula.

nodes.name: Interchange of monotone double limits
nodes.statement: If a scalar sequence $\{a_{n,m}\}_{n,m\geq1}$ is decreasing in both arguments, then $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}a_{n,m}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}a_{n,m}.$$
assumptions: If a scalar sequence $\{a_{n,m}\}_{n,m\geq1}$ is decreasing in both arguments, then

nodes.name: Monotonicity of regularized determinants under dyadic refinement
nodes.statement: Let $p_t\in\mathcal{M},$ $t\in[0,1],$ be an increasing net of projections with $p_0=0$ and $p_1=1$. Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the von Neumann subalgebra generated by $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n.$ If $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and $Tp_t=p_tTp_t$ for all $t\in[0,1]$, then $$\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)\geq \Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m).$$
nodes.statement_short: Refining the dyadic nest decreases $\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+1/m)$.
assumptions: Let $p_t\in\mathcal{M},$ $t\in[0,1],$ be an increasing net of projections with $p_0=0$ and $p_1=1$.
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the von Neumann subalgebra generated by $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n.$
If $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and $Tp_t=p_tTp_t$ for all $t\in[0,1]$, then

nodes.name: Proof of monotonicity under dyadic refinement
nodes.statement: We let $f_n^k=p_{(k+1)/2^n}-p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k<2^n$ and similarly $f_{n+1}^k=p_{(k+1)/2^{n+1}}-p_{k/2^{n+1}},$ $0\leq k<2^{n+1}$ . For an arbitrary $X\in\mathcal{M}$, we have \[ {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^n-1}f_n^kXf_n^k,\qquad {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}f_{n+1}^kXf_{n+1}^k. \] Note that $T$ is upper--triangular with respect to the list of projections $(f_n^k)_{0\le k<2^n}$ and $(f_{n+1}^k)_{0\le k<2^{n+1}}$ and, in particular, $f_{n+1}^{2k}$ is $f_n^kTf_n^k$-invariant and we may write $$f_n^kTf_n^k=\begin{pmatrix} f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}\\ 0&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k} \end{pmatrix}.$$ It follows from Corollary \ref{standard} and Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k+1}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k+1}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k+1})}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k})} \\ \leq\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)}. \end{multline*} It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\prod_{k=0}^{2^n-1}\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)} \\ \geq\prod_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^k\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^k}(|f_{n+1}^kTf_{n+1}^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_{n+1})}=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m) \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Each level-$n$ diagonal block is itself triangular over two level-$(n+1)$ blocks, so the determinant inequality applies blockwise and multiplies up.

nodes.name: Difference projections and expectation formulas
nodes.statement: We let $f_n^k=p_{(k+1)/2^n}-p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k<2^n$ and similarly $f_{n+1}^k=p_{(k+1)/2^{n+1}}-p_{k/2^{n+1}},$ $0\leq k<2^{n+1}$ . For an arbitrary $X\in\mathcal{M}$, we have \[ {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^n-1}f_n^kXf_n^k,\qquad {\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(X)=\sum_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}f_{n+1}^kXf_{n+1}^k. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write both commutant expectations as sums of corner compressions.

nodes.name: Refine one block
nodes.statement: Note that $T$ is upper--triangular with respect to the list of projections $(f_n^k)_{0\le k<2^n}$ and $(f_{n+1}^k)_{0\le k<2^{n+1}}$ and, in particular, $f_{n+1}^{2k}$ is $f_n^kTf_n^k$-invariant and we may write $$f_n^kTf_n^k=\begin{pmatrix} f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}\\ 0&f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k} \end{pmatrix}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Each level-$n$ block is upper triangular over its two level-$(n+1)$ children.

nodes.name: Blockwise determinant inequality
nodes.statement: It follows from Corollary \ref{standard} and Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k+1}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k+1}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k+1}Tf_{n+1}^{2k+1}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k+1})}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^{2k}\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^{2k}}(|f_{n+1}^{2k}Tf_{n+1}^{2k}|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f_{n+1}^{2k})} \\ \leq\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)}. \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the corollary and the triangular determinant formula to each block.

nodes.name: Multiply over blocks
nodes.statement: It follows now from Theorem~\ref{thm:det nu matrix} that \begin{multline*} \Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\prod_{k=0}^{2^n-1}\Delta_{f_n^k\mathcal{M}f_n^k}(|f_n^kTf_n^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_n)} \\ \geq\prod_{k=0}^{2^{n+1}-1}\Delta_{f_{n+1}^k\mathcal{M}f_{n+1}^k}(|f_{n+1}^kTf_{n+1}^k|^2+\frac1m)^{\tau(f^k_{n+1})}=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_{n+1}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m) \end{multline*}
nodes.statement_short: Take the trace-weighted product over all blocks to get the stated inequality.

nodes.name: Determinant is preserved by expectation onto the commutant of an invariant nest
nodes.statement: Let $p_t\in\mathcal{M},$ $t\in[0,1],$ be an increasing net of projections, continuous from the right, with $p_0=0$ and $p_1=1$ and let $\mathcal{D}$ be the von Neumann subalgebra generated by $\{p_t\mid t\in[0,1]\}.$ If $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and $Tp_t=p_tTp_t$ for all $t\in[0,1],$ then \begin{equation} \Delta(T)=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Delta(T)=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T))$ for an invariant right-continuous nest generating $\mathcal{D}$.
assumptions: Let $p_t\in\mathcal{M},$ $t\in[0,1],$ be an increasing net of projections, continuous from the right, with $p_0=0$ and $p_1=1$ and let $\mathcal{D}$ be the von Neumann subalgebra generated by $\{p_t\mid t\in[0,1]\}.$
If $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and $Tp_t=p_tTp_t$ for all $t\in[0,1],$ then

nodes.name: Proof that the determinant is preserved
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the algebra generated by the projections $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Using the continuity from the right of $p_t$, we get $\mathcal{D}'=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\mathcal{D}_n'$ and, by Lemma \ref{exp limit lemma}, we have $${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$$ in the strong operator topology. By Lemma \ref{vspom lemma}, the quantity $\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)$ is decreasing in $n$ and it is, trivially, also decreasing in $m.$ It follows from Lemma \ref{monotone triv} that \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m). \end{equation} Note that, by $T$-invariance of the projections $p_{k/2^n}$, using them to write $T$ as a block matrix of operators, yields an upper triangular matrix, and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$ is obtained by setting the non-diagonal blocks to zero. To compute the left hand side of \eqref{first exp}, Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} yields $\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=\Delta(T)$ and, thereby, we have $$\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=2\Delta(T).$$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we infer that the left hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta(T)$. To compute the right hand side of \eqref{first exp}, by Lemma 2.25 of \cite{HS1}, we have $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m).$$ Letting $m\to\infty,$ we infer that the right hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)).$ Thus, we have~\eqref{eq:DeltaD'T}.
nodes.statement_short: Swap the $n$ and $m$ limits of the doubly monotone quantity $\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+1/m)$ and evaluate both iterated limits.

nodes.name: Approximate $\mathcal{D}'$ by $\mathcal{D}_n'$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the algebra generated by the projections $p_{k/2^n},$ $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Using the continuity from the right of $p_t$, we get $\mathcal{D}'=\bigcap_{n\geq1}\mathcal{D}_n'$ and, by Lemma \ref{exp limit lemma}, we have $${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)=\lim_{n\to\infty}{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$$ in the strong operator topology.
nodes.statement_short: Right continuity gives $\mathcal{D}'=\bigcap\mathcal{D}_n'$ and strong convergence of the expectations.

nodes.name: Double monotonicity permits limit interchange
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{vspom lemma}, the quantity $\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)$ is decreasing in $n$ and it is, trivially, also decreasing in $m.$ It follows from Lemma \ref{monotone triv} that \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The quantity decreases in both $n$ and $m$, so the iterated limits agree.

nodes.name: Evaluate the left-hand iterated limit
nodes.statement: Note that, by $T$-invariance of the projections $p_{k/2^n}$, using them to write $T$ as a block matrix of operators, yields an upper triangular matrix, and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)$ is obtained by setting the non-diagonal blocks to zero. To compute the left hand side of \eqref{first exp}, Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} yields $\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=\Delta(T)$ and, thereby, we have $$\lim_{m\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=2\Delta(T).$$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we infer that the left hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta(T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangularity gives $\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T))=\Delta(T)$, so the left side is $2\Delta(T)$.

nodes.name: Evaluate the right-hand iterated limit
nodes.statement: To compute the right hand side of \eqref{first exp}, by Lemma 2.25 of \cite{HS1}, we have $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n'}(T)|^2+\frac1m)=\Delta(|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)|^2+\frac1m).$$ Letting $m\to\infty,$ we infer that the right hand side of \eqref{first exp} is $2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)).$ Thus, we have~\eqref{eq:DeltaD'T}.
nodes.statement_short: The right side is $2\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T))$, giving the identity.

nodes.name: Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ is small
nodes.statement: Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$ and let $\rho$, $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{D}_n$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. nodes.name: Proof that the dyadic remainder has small Brown measure
nodes.statement: The operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ when written as a matrix with respect to the nonzero projections from the list $(f^n_k)_{k=0}^{2^n-1}$ is upper triangular by Theorem \ref{thm:HS} \eqref{hsb} and has for diagonal entries \begin{equation} f^n_kTf^n_k-\frac{\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)}{\tau(f^n_k)}f^n_k. \end{equation} Repeating the argument in Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv} (see \eqref{trace partitioning}), we obtain, when $f^n_k\ne0$, that the Brown measure of $f^n_kTf^n_k$ in $f^n_k\mathcal{M}f^n_k$ is supported in $\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac{k+1}{2^n}])$ and $\tau(f^n_kTf^n_k)/\tau(f^n_k)$ lies in the convex hull of this set. Hence, the Brown measure of the difference \eqref{eq:fkdiagelt} is supported in the ball centered at the origin of radius $\operatorname{diam}(\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac {k+1}{2^n}]))$, which is no greater than $\omega(2^{-n}).$ Now applying Theorem \ref{thm:det nu matrix} $n$ times, we get that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ lies in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at the origin.
nodes.statement_short: Each diagonal entry of the remainder has Brown measure inside a disc of radius the arc diameter; the triangular splitting formula assembles them.

Hence, the Brown measure of the difference \eqref{eq:fkdiagelt} is supported in the ball centered at the origin of radius $\operatorname{diam}(\rho((\frac{k}{2^n},\frac {k+1}{2^n}]))$, which is no greater than $\omega(2^{-n}).$
nodes.statement_short: Each diagonal entry has Brown measure in a disc of radius at most $\omega(2^{-n})$.

nodes.name: Proof of the commuting case
nodes.statement: We assume without loss of generality $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2$. For every $n\geq0,$ let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the subalgebra of $\mathcal{D}$ generated by $q_{k/2^n}$, $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a unit vector $\eta\in H.$ By assumption, $T$ commutes with ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T).$ Since $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ commute, we have $$(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}=\sum_{k=0}^{2m}(-1)^k\binom{2m}{k}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k.$$ Since $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2,$ it follows that both ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ are contractions. For $k\leq m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)\|_{\infty}^m.$$ For $k>m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|.$$ Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv}, we have \begin{equation} \|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\eta\|\leq 2^{2m}\max\{\omega(2^{-n})^m,\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|\}. \end{equation} By Lemma \ref{brown small bound}, the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ is contained in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at $0.$ By the Haagerup--Schultz characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r}, for every unit vector $\xi\in H,$ there exists a sequence $\xi_m\to\xi$ such that $\|\xi_m\|=1$ and $$\limsup_{m\to\infty}\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq\omega(2^{-n}).$$ Hence, there exists $M$ (depending on $n$), such that $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|\leq (2\omega(2^{-n}))^m,\quad m>M.$$ Substituting $\xi_m$ for $\eta$ in \eqref{eq:TEpow}, we obtain $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq 8\omega(2^{-n}),\quad m>M.$$ Since $\xi$ was any unit vector, it follows from the characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r} of the Haagerup--Schultz subspace that the Brown measure of $(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^2$ is supported in the ball centered at $0$ of radius $8\omega(2^{-n}).$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$
nodes.statement_short: Binomially expand $(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}$ against the level-$n$ remainder, use the Haagerup--Schultz vector characterization, then let $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Normalization and setup
nodes.statement: We assume without loss of generality $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2$. For every $n\geq0,$ let $\mathcal{D}_n$ be the subalgebra of $\mathcal{D}$ generated by $q_{k/2^n}$, $0\leq k\leq 2^n$. Fix $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a unit vector $\eta\in H.$
nodes.statement_short: Rescale to $\|T\|_\infty\le1/2$ and fix a level $n$ and a unit vector.

nodes.name: Binomial expansion
nodes.statement: By assumption, $T$ commutes with ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T).$ Since $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ commute, we have $$(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}=\sum_{k=0}^{2m}(-1)^k\binom{2m}{k}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k.$$ Since $\|T\|_{\infty}\leq 1/2,$ it follows that both ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ and $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ are contractions.
nodes.statement_short: Commutativity lets us expand the $2m$-th power into products of the two remainders, both contractions.

nodes.name: Split the expansion by $k$
nodes.statement: For $k\leq m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)\|_{\infty}^m.$$ For $k>m,$ we have $$\|({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^{2m-k}(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^k\eta\|\leq\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|.$$ Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:Enormconv}, we have \begin{equation} \|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\eta\|\leq 2^{2m}\max\{\omega(2^{-n})^m,\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\eta\|\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound each term either by the norm remainder or by the operator remainder power.

nodes.name: Use the Haagerup--Schultz characterization
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{brown small bound}, the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T)$ is contained in the ball of radius $\omega(2^{-n})$ centered at $0.$ By the Haagerup--Schultz characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r}, for every unit vector $\xi\in H,$ there exists a sequence $\xi_m\to\xi$ such that $\|\xi_m\|=1$ and $$\limsup_{m\to\infty}\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq\omega(2^{-n}).$$ Hence, there exists $M$ (depending on $n$), such that $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}_n}(T))^m\xi_m\|\leq (2\omega(2^{-n}))^m,\quad m>M.$$
nodes.statement_short: Choose approximating unit vectors along which the level-$n$ remainder decays like $2\omega(2^{-n})$.

nodes.name: Conclude the Brown measure is $\delta_0$
nodes.statement: Substituting $\xi_m$ for $\eta$ in \eqref{eq:TEpow}, we obtain $$\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\xi_m\|^{1/m}\leq 8\omega(2^{-n}),\quad m>M.$$ Since $\xi$ was any unit vector, it follows from the characterization \eqref{eq:H-S H_r} of the Haagerup--Schultz subspace that the Brown measure of $(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^2$ is supported in the ball centered at $0$ of radius $8\omega(2^{-n}).$ Letting $n\to\infty,$ we obtain that the Brown measure of $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$
nodes.statement_short: Get $\|(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T))^{2m}\xi_m\|^{1/m}\le8\omega(2^{-n})$ and let $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5 (decomposition theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $q_t,$ $t\in[0,1],$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operators $Tq_t-\lambda$ and $(1-q_t)T-\lambda,$ we obtain \begin{align*} \Delta(Tq_t-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(Tq_t)-\lambda), \\ \Delta((1-q_t)T-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}((1-q_t)T-\lambda)). \end{align*} Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $Tq_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t)T$) equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)q_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t){\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$). In particular, the projection $q_t$ is the Haagerup--Schultz projection for ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ associated to the set $\rho([0,t]).$ By definition of $\mathcal{D}',$ the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)$ commutes with every $q_t.$ Hence, ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{comm quasinilpotent}. Since $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{D}'$ we have ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T))={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and by application of this lemma we infer that the Brown measure of the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$ Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda,$ we obtain $$\Delta(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda)=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda).$$ Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, i.e., it is $\delta_0$. Now letting $Q=T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and $N={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, we have $T=N+Q$ with $N$ normal and $Q$ s.o.t.-quasinilpotent. This proves Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decc}. Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decb} is already proved in Proposition \ref{br equ}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $q_t$ is also the Haagerup--Schultz nest of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$, apply the commuting case, and transport the conclusion back to $T$ via the determinant identity.

nodes.name: Reduce to the commutant expectation
nodes.statement: Let $q_t,$ $t\in[0,1],$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be as in Construction \ref{peano}. Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operators $Tq_t-\lambda$ and $(1-q_t)T-\lambda,$ we obtain \begin{align*} \Delta(Tq_t-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(Tq_t)-\lambda), \\ \Delta((1-q_t)T-\lambda)&=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}((1-q_t)T-\lambda)). \end{align*} Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $Tq_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t)T$) equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)q_t$ (respectively, of $(1-q_t){\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$). In particular, the projection $q_t$ is the Haagerup--Schultz projection for ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ associated to the set $\rho([0,t]).$ By definition of $\mathcal{D}',$ the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)$ commutes with every $q_t.$ Hence, ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$ satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma \ref{comm quasinilpotent}. Since $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{D}'$ we have ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T))={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and by application of this lemma we infer that the Brown measure of the operator ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ is $\delta_0.$
nodes.statement_short: Determinant identities show $q_t$ is the Haagerup--Schultz nest of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}'}(T)$, so the commuting case applies.

nodes.name: Transport back to $T$
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma \ref{first exp lemma} to the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda,$ we obtain $$\Delta(T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda)=\Delta({\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)-\lambda).$$ Hence, by \eqref{br def}, the Brown measure of the operator $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ equals that of ${\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D'}}(T)-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, i.e., it is $\delta_0$.
nodes.statement_short: The same identity shows $T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ has Brown measure $\delta_0$.

nodes.name: Assemble the decomposition
nodes.statement: Now letting $Q=T-{\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and $N={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$, we have $T=N+Q$ with $N$ normal and $Q$ s.o.t.-quasinilpotent. This proves Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decc}. Theorem \ref{decomposition} \eqref{decb} is already proved in Proposition \ref{br equ}.
nodes.statement_short: Set $N={\rm Exp}_{\mathcal{D}}(T)$ and $Q=T-N$; part (b) is the earlier proposition.

nodes.name: Proof of the $\log_+$ characterization
nodes.statement: We prove the if part first. For a given $u\in(0,1),$ set $t=\mu(u,A).$ We have $$\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,B)}{t})ds\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|B|}{t}))\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|A|}{t}))=\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds.$$ Hence, $B\prec\prec_{\log}A.$ We now prove the only if part. If $t>\|B\|_{\infty},$ then \eqref{eq:logAtBt} holds trivially, while if $t\le\|B\|_{\infty}$ then we have \begin{multline*} \tau(\log_+(\frac{|B|}{t}))=\int_0^{d_{|B|}(t)}\log(\frac{\mu(s,B)}{t})ds\leq\int_0^{d_{|B|}(t)}\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds \\ \leq\int_0^{d_{|A|}(t)}\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds=\tau(\log_+(\frac{|A|}{t})). \end{multline*}

nodes.statement_short: Both directions by choosing $t=\mu(u,A)$ respectively splitting at the distribution functions $d_{|B|}(t)\le d_{|A|}(t)$.

nodes.statement: We prove the if part first. For a given $u\in(0,1),$ set $t=\mu(u,A).$ We have $$\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,B)}{t})ds\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|B|}{t}))\leq\tau(\log_+(\frac{|A|}{t}))=\int_0^u\log(\frac{\mu(s,A)}{t})ds.$$ Hence, $B\prec\prec_{\log}A.$

nodes.name: Proof of stability under adding the identity
nodes.statement: By enlarging $\mathcal{M}$ if necessary, we may without loss of generality assume it is diffuse. Referring to Lemma \ref{boolean lemma}, we infer the existence of increasing nets $p_s,q_s$ $0\leq s\leq1,$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s,$ $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$B=\int_0^1\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad A=\int_0^1\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ Fix $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ and define the operators $$B_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad C_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,B)dp_s,\quad A_t=\int_0^t\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$ It is clear that $\mu(B_t)=\mu(C_t),$ $C_t\prec\prec_{\log} A_t$ and the operators $A_t,C_t$ are in the von Neumann algebra $p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$. Note that we have $\tau({\rm supp}(B_t))=\tau({\rm supp}(C_t))\le\tau({\rm supp}(A_t))$. Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B)),$ it follows that $A_t$ and $C_t$ are invertible and $\log(A_t),\log(C_t)\in p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$. Let $r=\max\{\|A_t^{-1}\|_{\infty},\|C_t^{-1}\|_{\infty}\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:log invertibles}, from $C_t\prec\prec_{\log}A_t$ we get $rC_t\prec\prec_{\log}rA_t$ and $\log(r C_t)\prec\prec\log(rA_t)$. Since the mapping $\Phi:z\to\log(1+r^{-1}e^z)$ is convex, it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \[ \int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,B))ds=\tau(\Phi(\log(rC_t)))\leq\tau(\Phi(\log(rA_t)))=\int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,A))ds. \] Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ is arbitrary, the assertion follows.

nodes.statement_short: Truncate $A$ and $B$ to a common corner, invert, and apply the Hardy--Littlewood--Polya inequality to the convex map $z\mapsto\log(1+r^{-1}e^z)$.

Referring to Lemma \ref{boolean lemma}, we infer the existence of increasing nets $p_s,q_s$ $0\leq s\leq1,$ of projections in $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\tau(p_s)=s,$ $\tau(q_s)=s$ and such that $$B=\int_0^1\mu(s,B)dq_s,\quad A=\int_0^1\mu(s,A)dp_s.$$

nodes.name: Truncate to a common corner

Note that we have $\tau({\rm supp}(B_t))=\tau({\rm supp}(C_t))\le\tau({\rm supp}(A_t))$.

nodes.name: Pass to logarithms
nodes.statement: Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B)),$ it follows that $A_t$ and $C_t$ are invertible and $\log(A_t),\log(C_t)\in p_t\mathcal{M}p_t$. Let $r=\max\{\|A_t^{-1}\|_{\infty},\|C_t^{-1}\|_{\infty}\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:log invertibles}, from $C_t\prec\prec_{\log}A_t$ we get $rC_t\prec\prec_{\log}rA_t$ and $\log(r C_t)\prec\prec\log(rA_t)$.

nodes.statement_short: Invertibility and the scaling lemma give $\log(rC_t)\prec\prec\log(rA_t)$.

nodes.name: Apply convexity and let $t$ increase
nodes.statement: Since the mapping $\Phi:z\to\log(1+r^{-1}e^z)$ is convex, it follows from Theorem \ref{hlp theorem} that \[ \int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,B))ds=\tau(\Phi(\log(rC_t)))\leq\tau(\Phi(\log(rA_t)))=\int_0^t\log(1+\mu(s,A))ds. \] Since $t<\tau({\rm supp}(B))$ is arbitrary, the assertion follows.

nodes.statement_short: Convexity plus Hardy--Littlewood--Polya gives the inequality for every $t$.

nodes.name: Weyl inequality for the normal part in the II$_1$--setting
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a diffuse, finite von Neumann algebra and let $\tau$ be a normal, faithful, tracial state on $\mathcal{M}$. Let $T\in\mathcal{M}$. If $N\in\mathcal{M}$ is the normal operator constructed by means of Theorem \ref{decomposition}, then \begin{enumerate}[{\rm (a)}] \item $N\prec\prec_{\log}T.$ \item for every increasing real valued function $\Phi$ on $[0,\infty)$ so that $\Phi\circ\exp$ is convex, we have \begin{equation} \int\Phi(|z|)\,d\mu_T(z)=\tau(\Phi(|N|))\leq\tau(\Phi(|T|)). \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: A Weyl inequality in the II$_1$--setting
nodes.statement_short: The normal part $N$ is logarithmically submajorized by $T$, whence $\int\Phi(|z|)d\mu_T=\tau(\Phi(|N|))\le\tau(\Phi(|T|))$.
